candidates.text:
Standard: 1.T.C.2
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Identify who is speaking or telling the story at different points in a text.
Skills:
- Identify who is speaking at various points in a text.
Observable behaviors:
- Point out the speaker or narrator in a story.
- Recognize changes in who is speaking during a text.
- Name the person or character telling the story at various parts.
Pedagogy terms: speaker identification, narrator, point of view, text roles
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify the speaker or narrator in a text.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain who is speaking at different points in a text.
- comprehension_response: Respond to questions about who is telling the story.
Codes: 1.T.C.2
candidates.label: Authors & Speakers

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.T.T.1.a
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK1_recall_reproduction
Competency: Identify story elements such as characters, setting, major events, and dialogue used to craft stories.
Skills:
- Identify characters used to craft a story.
- Identify the setting used to craft a story.
- Identify major events used to craft a story.
- Identify dialogue used to craft a story.
Observable behaviors:
- Point out characters in a story.
- Describe the setting of a story.
- Identify major events in a story.
- Recognize dialogue between characters in a story.
Pedagogy terms: characters, setting, major events, dialogue, story elements
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify story elements such as characters, setting, major events, and dialogue in a story.
Codes: 1.T.T.1.a

Standard: 1.P.EICC.2.c
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing, Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Explain ideas and learn new concepts by interpreting and creating texts.
Skills:
- Explain concepts by interpreting texts.
- Learn concepts by interpreting texts.
- Construct texts to demonstrate understanding of concepts and processes.
Observable behaviors:
- Explain ideas based on information from texts.
- Construct texts to demonstrate understanding of concepts and processes.
- Interpret information from texts to learn new concepts.
Pedagogy terms: interpret texts, construct texts, explain concepts, learn from texts
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify concepts and processes in texts.
- oral_production: Explain concepts and processes orally based on texts.
- written_production: Write explanations and construct texts to show understanding.
- procedural_application: Use texts to explain and learn concepts and processes.
- representation_modeling: Construct texts to represent understanding of concepts and processes.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain concepts and processes by interpreting texts.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by explaining and learning concepts and processes.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.2.c

Standard: 1.T.T.2.a
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Identify techniques used to create expository texts, including recognizing the main topic and supporting details.
Skills:
- Identify the main topic in an expository text.
- Identify supporting details in an expository text.
- Recognize techniques used to craft expository texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Point out the main topic in an expository text.
- Identify supporting details that explain or describe the main topic.
- Recognize techniques authors use to organize and present information in expository texts.
Pedagogy terms: expository text, main topic, supporting details, text features, text structure
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify the main topic and supporting details in expository texts.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how supporting details relate to the main topic in an expository text.
- comprehension_response: Describe the main topic and supporting details when reading expository texts.
Codes: 1.T.T.2.a

Standard: 1.P.ST.1.c
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Explore how the context influences the author's choices and how the audience responds when interpreting and creating texts.
Skills:
- Explore how context shapes the author's decisions when interpreting texts.
- Explore how context shapes the audience's responses when interpreting texts.
- Explore how context shapes the author's decisions when constructing texts.
- Explore how context shapes the audience's responses when constructing texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Discuss how background information or cultural influences affect a story or text.
- Identify ways the time period or location shapes the author's decisions.
- Describe how understanding context helps explain audience reactions to a text.
Pedagogy terms: context, author's purpose, audience response, interpretation, text construction
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify elements of context such as background, location, culture, or time period in texts.
- oral_production: Discuss how context influences author decisions and audience responses.
- procedural_application: Explore and apply knowledge of context to interpret and construct texts.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how context shapes author choices and audience reactions.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by considering how context affects meaning and interpretation.
Codes: 1.P.ST.1.c

Standard: 1.P.EICC.3
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Vocabulary
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Students engage with complex texts for different purposes by using comprehension strategies before, during, and after reading to understand and make meaning.
Skills:
- Establish a purpose and set goals for reading
- Monitor comprehension and adjust strategies as needed
- Scan and skim the text to note useful structures and sections
- Draw from and integrate prior knowledge with the text, addressing inconsistencies or gaps
- Summarize and visualize sections of the text to maintain understanding
- Make and track predictions about upcoming events and information
- Make, track, and support inferences about different levels of meaning
- Determine meanings of unfamiliar words and concepts using context, academic vocabulary, and word parts
Observable behaviors:
- Set a purpose and goals for reading a text
- Monitor understanding while reading and adjust strategies as needed
- Scan and skim texts to identify useful structures and sections
- Connect prior knowledge to new information in the text and resolve inconsistencies
- Summarize and create mental images of text sections to maintain understanding
- Make and track predictions about upcoming events or information in the text
- Make, track, and support inferences about meanings within the text
- Determine meanings of unfamiliar words using context, academic vocabulary, and word parts
Pedagogy terms: comprehension strategies, monitor comprehension, set reading goals, scan and skim, prior knowledge, summarize, visualize, predict, infer, context clues, academic vocabulary, word parts
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify text structures and unfamiliar words using context and word parts
- procedural_application: Apply comprehension strategies such as setting goals, monitoring understanding, scanning, summarizing, predicting, and inferring while reading
- representation_modeling: Visualize and summarize sections of text to support understanding
- reasoning_explanation: Explain inferences and predictions about text meaning and events
- comprehension_response: Summarize text sections and track comprehension progress
Codes: 1.P.EICC.3
candidates.label: Comprehension Strategies

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.T.T.1.d
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: With adult support, compare and contrast characters and their experiences in stories from different cultures.
Skills:
- Compare characters in stories from diverse cultures with adult support.
- Contrast characters in stories from diverse cultures with adult support.
- Compare experiences of characters in stories from diverse cultures with adult support.
- Contrast experiences of characters in stories from diverse cultures with adult support.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify characters in stories from diverse cultures.
- Describe experiences of characters in different stories.
- Discuss similarities and differences between characters and their experiences across stories.
Pedagogy terms: compare and contrast, characters, experiences, stories, diverse cultures, adult support
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize characters and their experiences in stories from diverse cultures with adult support.
- oral_production: Describe and discuss similarities and differences between characters and their experiences in stories with adult support.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how characters and their experiences are similar or different across stories with adult support.
- comprehension_response: Compare and contrast characters and their experiences in stories from diverse cultures with adult support.
Codes: 1.T.T.1.d

Standard: 1.T.C.1
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing, Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Explain how authors use language to achieve a specific purpose and address a target audience, and create texts in various modes.
Skills:
- Identify the general purpose of a variety of texts.
- Identify the target audience of a variety of texts.
- Identify different modes of communication: print, digital, auditory, and visual.
- Create texts in teacher-selected modes such as print, digital, auditory, and/or visual.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify the general purpose of a text, such as telling stories, providing information, sharing opinions, or explaining ideas.
- Recognize the target audience for different texts.
- Identify different modes of communication including print, digital, auditory, and visual.
- Create texts using teacher-selected modes such as print, digital, auditory, or visual formats.
Pedagogy terms: purpose, audience, modes of communication, text creation
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify the general purpose and target audience in various texts and recognize different modes of communication.
- written_production: Create texts in teacher-selected modes such as print or digital.
- representation_modeling: Create texts in teacher-selected modes including auditory and visual formats.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how authors use language for a specific purpose and target audience.
Codes: 1.T.C.1
candidates.label: Purpose & Audience

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.T.T.1.c
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Describe the main characters' traits and explain how their words and actions support the story's central message, lesson, or moral.
Skills:
- Describe traits of the main characters.
- Explain how the characters' words support the central message, lesson, or moral.
- Explain how the characters' actions support the central message, lesson, or moral.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify main characters in a story.
- Describe traits of main characters.
- Explain how characters' words and actions relate to the story's message, lesson, or moral.
Pedagogy terms: main characters, character traits, central message, lesson, moral, words and actions, explanation
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify main characters and their traits in a story.
- oral_production: Explain orally how characters' words and actions support the story's message, lesson, or moral.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how the characters' words and actions support the central message, lesson, or moral of the story.
- comprehension_response: Describe traits of main characters and explain their connection to the story's message, lesson, or moral.
Codes: 1.T.T.1.c

Standard: 1.T.T.2.b
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: none
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Describe how two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text are connected.
Skills:
- Describe the connection between two individuals in a text.
- Describe the connection between two events in a text.
- Describe the connection between two ideas in a text.
- Describe the connection between two pieces of information in a text.
Observable behaviors:
- Explain how two characters in a story relate to each other.
- Describe how one event leads to another in a text.
- Identify connections between two ideas presented in a text.
- Point out relationships between two pieces of information in a text.
Pedagogy terms: text connections, relationships, cause and effect, compare and contrast
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify connections between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
- oral_production: Describe aloud the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
- written_production: Write or draw to show the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain the relationship between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
- comprehension_response: Respond to questions about how two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text are connected.
Codes: 1.T.T.2.b
